name: The Vietnam War: From Indochina to Saigon
description: How French colonial rule, a Cold War divide and American escalation led to thirty years of war, and what the conflict left behind.

checkpoints.name: French rule and revolt
checkpoints.note: France joined its colonies into French Indochina. Ho Chi Minh, who later led the independence movement, and the officer Vo Nguyen Giap built a movement that declared Vietnam independent in 1945.

checkpoints.name: The first war
checkpoints.note: France fought the First Indochina War against the Viet Minh. It ended with the French defeat at the Battle of Dien Bien Phu in 1954, after which Vietnam was divided into a north and a south.

checkpoints.name: The Americans arrive
checkpoints.note: South Vietnam was founded, backed by the United States in its Cold War contest with communism, while the north looked to communist allies. President John F. Kennedy sent more advisers, and the war grew.

checkpoints.name: Escalation
checkpoints.note: President Lyndon B. Johnson sent combat troops. American forces used B-52 bombers and napalm, while their opponents carried AK-47 rifles. The Tet Offensive of 1968 shook American confidence, the war divided opinion at home, and Richard Nixon began to withdraw troops.

checkpoints.name: The aftermath
checkpoints.note: Fighting ended in 1975 and the country was reunited soon after. Watergate had weakened Nixon, and in neighbouring Cambodia Pol Pot ruled through the Khmer Rouge. Apocalypse Now, released in 1979, helped shape how the war is remembered.
